boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Fairfax Campus settings for silent reading, collaborative work, research, presentations, and technology-assisted assignments, with access constraints noted.

cards.title: Start in the Two-Story Atrium
cards.subtitle: Open study space beside Fenwick Library’s main service hub
cards.notes: Settle into the open atrium for a flexible work session, then use the nearby Information Desk when research or navigation questions arise.
cards.short_summary: An open, two-story setting that pairs study seating with immediate library help.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason University Libraries identifies the Fenwick Atrium as an open, two-story space containing study spaces, laptop checkout, library materials, and the Information Desk.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Fenwick Library; enter during the library's posted operating hours. Some equipment and borrowing services require Mason credentials.

cards.title: Spread Out in the Research Commons
cards.subtitle: Second-floor study choices near research support
cards.notes: Choose this second-floor commons when you want multiple seating options and quick access to computers, research consultations, or production support.
cards.short_summary: A flexible second-floor study area surrounded by specialized research services.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Fenwick Library tour says the second-floor Research Commons offers a variety of study spaces and public computers near SP@RC, subject librarians, and other research services.
cards.access_notes: Located on Fenwick Library's second floor and available during posted library hours; individual services may require appointments.

cards.title: Read Quietly in the Music Library
cards.subtitle: A quiet second-floor space among music collections
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from quiet, and use the surrounding scores, books, and recordings when your project touches music.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study seating embedded in Fenwick’s specialized music collection.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason University Libraries explicitly describes the Music Library as a quiet study space and says it houses scores, books, and audio and video recordings.
cards.source_title: Fenwick Library Tour - Music Library and Data & Digital Scholarship Services
cards.access_notes: Located on Fenwick Library's second floor and usable during posted library hours; borrowing privileges depend on library eligibility.

cards.title: Build a Data-Heavy Project Here
cards.subtitle: Active collaborative study with specialized software and expertise
cards.notes: Use this active workspace for GIS, data analysis, or digital-humanities work, and arrange a consultation when the tools become the assignment.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative research setting for computational and data-centered coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes Data & Digital Scholarship Services as an active study space with collaborative areas, specialized software and technology, consultations, and workshops.
cards.source_title: Fenwick Library Tour - Music Library and Data & Digital Scholarship Services
cards.access_notes: Located on Fenwick Library's second floor. Collaborative space is available during library hours; consultations and workshops may require advance scheduling.

cards.title: Find Silence by the Compact Shelves
cards.subtitle: A designated silent-study area on Fenwick’s third floor
cards.notes: Head to the third-floor compact shelving area for individual work, follow the posted silent-zone expectations, and choose a nearby study space.
cards.short_summary: A clearly designated silent area tucked among Fenwick’s movable stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The official library tour says Fenwick's third floor is primarily quiet study space and that study rooms and spaces in the compact-shelving areas are designated for silent study.
cards.access_notes: Available during Fenwick Library hours. Observe the posted silent-study designation and follow instructions before moving compact shelving.

cards.title: Go Fully Silent in Room 5003
cards.subtitle: A fifth-floor reading room reserved for graduate students
cards.notes: Graduate students can bring concentration-heavy reading here; confirm fifth-floor eligibility and preserve the room’s explicitly silent setting.
cards.short_summary: A graduate-only silent reading room for focused individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason University Libraries identifies Room 5003 as the Graduate Student Silent Reading Room within Fenwick's fifth-floor Graduate Student Research Spaces.
cards.source_title: Fenwick Library Tour - Graduate Student Research Spaces
cards.access_notes: Graduate students only. The room is on Fenwick's fifth floor and is available subject to the library's posted hours and graduate-space rules.

cards.title: Use the Open North Study Area
cards.subtitle: A two-story, 20-seat study and research space
cards.notes: Pick this open-plan area for reading or research when you want a defined study zone without booking a room; seating is not reservable.
cards.short_summary: An open, two-level study area designed for reading and research.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes Fenwick's North Study Area as a 600-square-foot, two-story study-research space with open seating for 20 and marks it as not reservable.
cards.source_title: Your Support Can Build A Library for the Future
cards.access_notes: Inside Fenwick Library and available during posted building hours. The official space description marks the area as not reservable.

cards.title: Rehearse the Presentation, Not Just the Slides
cards.subtitle: A technology-supported room for teams of up to five
cards.notes: Reserve this third-floor room for a timed rehearsal, load your visuals in advance, and let every group member practice using the equipment.
cards.short_summary: A small, technology-equipped room purpose-built for presentation rehearsal.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason University describes Fenwick's third-floor Presentation Practice Room as a 150-square-foot technology-supported rehearsal space accommodating five students.
cards.source_title: Your Support Can Build A Library for the Future
cards.access_notes: Reservation required. University Libraries limits its study rooms to Mason students, faculty, or staff with a valid Mason NetID.

cards.title: Book a Johnson Center Study Room
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms for group assignments and virtual classes
cards.notes: Reserve with your NetID for a group assignment or virtual class, and plan within the four-hour daily limit and 14-day booking window.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms with clearly stated limits for structured group work.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason Student Centers says Johnson Center study rooms support group assignments and virtual classes; eligible Mason users may reserve once daily for up to four hours, up to 14 days ahead.
cards.access_notes: Only Mason students, faculty, and staff may reserve, and a valid Mason NetID is required. Reservations are limited to four hours per day.

cards.title: Pair Group Study with Software Help
cards.subtitle: The CLUB combines collaboration space with technical assistance
cards.notes: Bring a team assignment that depends on campus software, work collaboratively, and use the available assistance when a technical step stalls progress.
cards.short_summary: A technology-oriented collaborative workspace with software assistance nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: George Mason Information Technology Services identifies the Collaborative Learning Hub, or CLUB, as a software-assistance and group collaborative study space available on the Fairfax Campus.
cards.source_title: What IT resources are available at Mason?
cards.access_notes: Intended for Mason technology-supported work on the Fairfax Campus. Check the linked service information for current availability and assistance coverage.

warnings: The fixed board title is editorial framing; no card claims that these spaces are crowded or occupied by 9 a.m.
Coordinates and maps URLs are null because exact room-level coordinates were not verified from the supporting pages.
Fenwick North Study Area and Presentation Practice Room details come from an official university space-description page that does not display a publication date.
